description: This line plot illustrates how three distinct accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Initial Accuracy, and Δ Accuracy—vary as a function of Initial Confidence, which is plotted on the x-axis ranging from approximately 0.88 to 1.00 in linear scale, labeled “Initial Confidence.” The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear scale. The “Final Accuracy” is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, starting at approximately 1.00 and remaining nearly constant near that value across the entire range. The “Initial Accuracy” is depicted by a dashed green line with square markers, beginning at approximately 0.65, rising to a peak of approximately 0.95 around an Initial Confidence of 0.97, then declining slightly to about 0.93. The “Δ Accuracy,” shown as an orange dashed line with diamond markers, begins at approximately 0.30, dips slightly to about 0.25, then rises steadily to approximately 0.80 by the end of the range. All lines are accompanied by error bars indicating variability.
